title: From the Editor — Issue 02
settingText: The familiar bright maintained station break room before lunch: one cheerful chair pointing unnecessarily toward a taped microwave, a personal mug coaster beside a shared cup shelf, a clean rag left by a bin, and the quiet window nook whose chair has been moved. Dry workplace comedy, no people, no invented readable environmental text.
summary: Primary composition: single full-page editorial splash in a bright maintained Stardust Station workplace. Use setting and props for dry workplace comedy, reserve generous negative space for exact integrated editorial copy, and keep the story resolution off the image.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic full-bleed illustration rather than sequential story panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy; the environment and typography should feel composed together.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook. Do not invent additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Every workplace has a break room.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It's where people go when they want five minutes away from work.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Unfortunately, their coworkers had the same idea.

directionInline.text: This is an interior editorial/interstitial comic page, not a cover or dossier. Preserve Stardust Station's bright polished workplace-science-fiction visual language: clean maintained StarTrust surfaces, practical workplace clutter, ordinary human-scale spaces and dry visual comedy. No generic cyberpunk, grimdark, mystical effects or sacred-material framing.

Treat every CAPTION entry as exact integrated editorial typography, not speech balloons. Preserve wording, punctuation and order exactly. If long copy cannot render reliably, preserve the successful artwork with a clean reserved text field and correct the lettering separately rather than paraphrasing or shortening the copy.
No spoilers beyond the supplied editorial copy. Let setting, props and composition suggest pressure without visually depicting the story solution, reveal or outcome.

source: Star Splitter Visions editorial framing, revised 2026-10-10
